items.item: Modern engines prefer quicksort run generation over replacement selection because the cost model counts block transfers, not the scattered-memory-access comparisons that dominate on real hardware

items.item: A k-way merge using a min-heap (or loser tree) of each run's front item folds all runs down in a single pass, at about log2(k) comparisons per output item but only one read and one write of each block

items.item: A cascade (two-way) merge of k runs needs about log2(k) passes over all the data, which a single k-way merge pass avoids entirely

items.item: Fan-in is set by memory divided by block size minus one (for the output buffer), and the pass count is 1 + the ceiling of log base fan-in of the run count

items.item: Splitting a fixed memory budget across a larger fan-in shrinks each run's read buffer, which can turn sequential reads into seeks and make a lower pass count slower in wall-clock time
